figures.subdivisions: One perspective apparatus; no subfigure letters.
figures.location: Upper right of page; drawing roughly x974..1240, y278..774; separate caption below around y830..859.
inventory: Tall inverted-U/horseshoe magnet in perspective: curved bridge, two upright legs, outlined right outer face and densely black left inner/front face; lower pole shoes face the gap.
Dark perspective rectangular coil/frame sits between the two lower pole regions, with front/lower and rear/upper edges, winding/axle strokes and substantial black scan texture.

Horizontal shaft/contact assembly projects left of the coil: adjacent oval ring/collar forms, contacts/brush strokes, and two separately descending irregular lead strokes with small looped portions and free lower ends.
A small filled curved rotation/pointer-shaped stroke lies above and to the left of the outer shaft end. Preserve its curve and head as drawn; no full added circular arrow.

A clear N-shaped pole mark is next to the lower right gap/pole. The opposite pole has tiny light/dark letter-like marks in the heavily shaded region; preserve these shapes without assigning an unsupported encoded glyph.
Magnet, coil, rings/contacts, rotation mark and both dangling leads must all survive the crop. No drawn meter, external closed circuit, extra terminal, or added pole label is visible.
figures.boundary: Left page prose is outside the apparatus. Caption is separate below its lowest leads; do not include prose or cut leads to remove caption.
limitations: Dense black shading hides some internal contacts and the opposite-pole glyph identity. Ring/brush connectivity is recorded as visible apparatus shapes, not an invented circuit netlist.

Right capacitor has two separated, thick horizontal perspective plate shapes with slanted ends; top wire meets upper plate and lower plate connects to bottom wire.

The capacitor gap remains open between plates while the coil/conductors form the complete LC circuit.

figures.subdivisions: Two adjacent selector circuits share one a-shaped subdivision mark centered beneath the pair; spring/mass at right has a separate be-shaped subdivision mark. Do not label the two circuits as distinct a/b panels.
figures.location: Bottom drawing band roughly x206..1253, y1724..1980; caption below near x674..786, y1983..2010; printed page footer is lower and separate.
inventory: LEFT selector circuit: left branch has two cell symbols (each long thin upper horizontal stroke and short thick lower stroke), separated by a dashed vertical continuation; bottom conductor runs rightward to coil return with a central capacitor-bottom junction.

LEFT top battery lead ends at contact 1. Separate contact 2 leads rightward to a four-lobed vertical coil. A slanted selector blade connects the capacitor-top circular pivot to contact 1, leaving contact 2 disconnected.

LEFT capacitor: two thick horizontal plates; four plus-shaped marks just below the upper plate and four short horizontal minus-shaped marks above the lower plate. A q-like charge glyph with small M-shaped subscript is to the upper right; a separate leading minus and q-like/M-shaped group is to the lower right.

RIGHT selector circuit: same two-cell left branch, dashed continuation, bottom conductor, central capacitor-bottom junction and four-lobed right coil. Contact 1 on the battery lead is open; the slanted blade runs from capacitor-top circular pivot up-right to contact 2, closing the capacitor/coil path while the battery top is disconnected.

RIGHT capacitor again has four upper plus marks and four lower horizontal minus marks, upper q-like/M-shaped group and lower leading-minus q-like/M-shaped group. Do not replace the marks with dots, remove them, reverse polarity, or add voltage/current labels.

Both circuits retain the contact numerals 1 and 2 above their respective contacts, circular switch pivots, distinct blade orientations, plate gaps, bottom junctions, cell strokes and exact shared subdivision.

RIGHT mechanical drawing: short horizontally striped support, vertical attachment, continuous angular zigzag spring with about five prominent rightward teeth and a small initial bend, then a round heavily shaded mass below the equilibrium line.

A long broken horizontal equilibrium/reference stroke begins just right of the second circuit, crosses the spring near its lower attachment, and continues right of it. It is separate from the circuit, not an electrical conductor joined to the coil.

A second, lower horizontal stroke runs from the mass toward the right and ends in a small right-pointing shape. A vertical displacement/reference stroke to the right crosses both levels and extends above and below them, with thick arrowhead-like portions at upper/lower locations.

Two small glyph groups lie just left of that vertical stroke: an upper tiny tilted/two-level mark and a lower x-like mark. Retain their actual positions/shapes without guessing Latin/Cyrillic or exact subscript identity.
The equilibrium label is physically below the broken line between circuit and spring. Its text transcription belongs to D269; here its crop presence/boundary alone is recorded.

No plotted sinusoidal curve, graph axes/grid, extra terminal, separately named mass, or added displacement value is visible. The visible curves are the coil lobes, rounded mass and spring/arrow strokes.
figures.boundary: Charge labels at right of both capacitors, numerals above switches, both subdivision marks, full arrow tails and equilibrium label belong to this drawing region. Main figure caption is below; surrounding equation/body prose above and page footer below are not diagram strokes.
limitations: The source crop enlarges existing pixels only. Tiny upper displacement glyph and small arrowhead contours cannot establish encoded glyph identity or a precise numeric displacement.
Spring tooth count is visually approximate because attachment bends are not separate turns; preserve the complete observed zigzag rather than normalize its count.
Black plate/brush texture and small white scan holes remain source texture, not inferred new contacts or terminals.

rawPolicy: Retain original subdivisions, marks and source texture as shapes. Impossible Latin/Cyrillic encoded identity is not a RAW fidelity demand. Modern language/culture/type-size gates are outside this review.
